Players are ranked by their average finish across the heroes they play, each finish weighted by how much it's worth trusting: a deeper pool counts for more (#1 of 20 over #1 of 3, saturating around 7 opponents — past that, deeper fields in this group are not stronger ones), and a hero you've actually played counts for more than one that only just cleared the display floor. Finishing position itself is never rewritten by pool size — 7th of 36 is 7th of 36. That average is then pulled toward the middle of the board by how much evidence backs it, so breadth and volume decide who leads when two records are close — but a thin record is only ever held back from the top, never pushed below a worse one. The Avg finish chip on each profile is the raw, unadjusted figure. The standing itself is an exact place — players who score equally are separated by their average finish, so no two share one. A player carrying less than one fully-credible hero's worth of evidence is shown with a — instead of a place: not enough to rank them, which is not the same as a low rank.

Teammate synergy

Who wins together, at every stack size — toggle Duo / Trio / Quad / 5-stack / 6-stack above. Games and win rate together per mode, and Lift — the group's actual win rate minus the rate expected from the members' records outside the group (in points; descriptive, not causal: stacks also choose when and against whom they queue). Click a group's row (▸) to drill in: Hero combos (each member's hero that match, one column per player) or Maps — click a member's name to go straight to their profile instead.

How to read these tables

Groups need 5+ shared games to appear, and a mode shows — until it has 5 games of its own; Lift needs 10+ (a stricter floor — a 5-game sample is too thin for its own shrink to fully tame). Bars, printed rates and sorting all use the raw rate; hover a rate for its sample-shrunk twin (short lucky runs discounted), and * marks modes under 20 games.

Sizes overlap in these tables (unlike the stack-size pills above them, where each team counts once at its exact size — so a match where tracked players faced each other reads once for each side, and none of those sizes separates from the solo baseline once you account for how few games the deeper stacks have): a group's games count every match those players shared a team, so a 6-stack's games also appear in every duo, trio, quad and 5-stack inside it.

The Best hero pairings section further down has its own Lift column: same idea, different comparison — a hero PAIR against the two heroes' other duo line-ups, not a player group against its members' records apart.

In the drilldown, hero line-ups that occurred only once roll up into a one-off tally below the table.

Win rate by stack size — each team counted once, at its exact size. 2 of 5 separate from the solo baseline at the bar a family of 5 needs; the rest are inside their own noise.

Squad matchups

The squad's record when the enemy team fields a hero (each enemy at their primary hero that match), QM + Competitive, over 990,375 hero-encounters — the group-level read that the per-player Matchups strips are now scored against. Baseline: the squad wins 49.8% of these; the 56 heroes span 14.7pp, from Storm 43.5% 8,807g up to Black Widow 58.2% 8,323g. Unlike the per-player cells — where no gap survives a 5% false-discovery correction — this spread is far too large and too deep to be chance.

Two caveats that the size of the numbers does not remove. Counting grain: a lobby is folded once per tracked player in it, so a stacked match counts several times — the counts are inflated and the rows are correlated (the rates are unaffected in expectation). Descriptive, not causal: who the enemy picks tracks map, mode and rank band, so a low row says the squad tends to lose lobbies that hero shows up in — not that the hero counters them. Rows under 100 encounters are omitted; hover a Win % for its sample-shrunk rate. Click a hero to open its page.

Squad record book

Group-level bests over the squad's stored history — every match with a tracked player counts once, whoever played (126,578 stored matches; a floor of the true total). Days are the store's dates (UTC). Under the day and stretch cards the QM/Comp line splits that same window by mode and adds back to it; under the two streak cards it is each mode's own longest run, which can be longer than the all-modes streak above it because the other mode's games are skipped rather than breaking it. "Best" day/stretch are ranked by win rate (shrunk toward 50% for small samples), not raw win count — a losing record can never win either slot; the W–L shown is always the real, unshrunk record.
